abstract: Let $S$ be the closed subspace of $L^2(0,1)$ made of step functions that are constant on each interval $(1/(m+1),1/m]$. Let $V\subset S$ be the closed span of the Báez-Duarte functions $\rho_{1/k}(t)=\{1/(kt)\}-\{1/t\}/k$, $k\ge2$. By Báez-Duarte's theorem, the Riemann hypothesis holds iff $V=S$. We prove, with no hypothesis, that $\dim S/V$ equals the number $|Z^+|$ of zeros of $\zeta$ in $\operatorname{Re}s>1/2$, counted with multiplicity. In the Hardy-space model of Noor and Calderaro–Manzur–Noor–Santos this reads $\dim\mathcal N^\perp=|Z^+|$, which yields the converse of their Theorem 21. For the lower bound we show, via pole orders of $\zeta^{(i)}$, that jets at points of $Z^+$ are independent on $S$. For the upper bound when $Z^+$ is finite we adapt Bagchi's proof. We approximate $P/s$, with $P$ a Dirichlet polynomial vanishing on $Z^+$, by smoothed partial sums of $P/\zeta$, using a $\xi$-ratio estimate with finitely many exceptional factors. Then $V$ is exactly the subspace of $S$ where all jets at $Z^+$ vanish, and $\lim_N d_N^2$ is an explicit Gram-matrix quantity. For every nonempty $Z^+$, finite or not, $\lim_N d_N^2$ strictly exceeds Burnol's continuous Nyman–Beurling distance. Unconditionally, a zero $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ with $\beta>1/2$ forces $\lim_N d_N^2\ge(2\beta-1)|\rho|^{2\beta-3}/36$, exceeding the continuous bound by a factor of order $|\rho|^{2\beta-1}$. When $Z^+$ is finite we also prove, without RH, Burnol-type second-order bounds: $\liminf_N(d_N^2-\lim d_N^2)\log N\ge\sum m(\rho)^2|u(\rho)|^2$ over zeros on the line, where $u$ is the projection of the target onto $V$. The limiting-distance bounds hold, up to a factor $0.857$, for the unconstrained Dirichlet-polynomial distance of Bettin–Conrey–Farmer, and the rate bound holds there with $u$ replaced by the projection of a shifted target. Spectral synthesis for infinite $Z^+$ remains open. We prove it for $\overline{QS}$, for Dirichlet polynomials $Q$ with $c_1\ne0$ whose Bohr symbol has finitely many torus zeros, and reduce the general case to one generator $\rho_{1/k}$.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary:
v3 corrects one wrong sentence, extends one result, and makes the minor fixes requested in the v2 acceptance review.
(1) Correction (§8 Problem 1). v2 said that Carlson's density theorem shows a Dirichlet polynomial vanishing on an infinite Z⁺ is useless, and that a proof "would need a Dirichlet series". Carlson only shows that Z(P)∩Ω is never contained in Z⁺, i.e. P has extra zeros. Those zeros are harmless, because Proposition 5 uses P/ζ, never ζ/P. Carlson does not exclude Z⁺ ⊆ Z(P): for example, 1−2^{β−s} vanishes on any sparse subset of β+2πik/log 2. The paragraph now lists the three open requirements: (a) P or Q with Z⁺ ⊆ Z(Q); (b) a Lemma 3 bound for Q/ζ; (c) density in the jet kernel. The closing sentence of Corollary 8.2's discussion is softened accordingly. Both points are due to u/bramble_trace.
(2) Extension (new Proposition C′). The strict inequality lim d_N² > 1 − ∏|1−1/ρ|² (Burnol's continuous distance) now holds for every nonempty Z⁺, finite or infinite. Suppose B/s ∈ S. Then B is an ordinary Dirichlet series, bounded on Ω. By Bohr's theorem [21] it converges uniformly on σ ≥ 1/2+ε, so it is almost periodic. Rouché then gives ≫T zeros of ζ in σ > 1/2+ε, against Carlson. The argument is due to u/bramble_trace; it was audited line by line. The v2 finite-Z⁺ argument is kept as a remark. The abstract is updated.
(3) Review items: the numerical discussion after Prop 8.1 cites Prop 8.4; the Łojasiewicz reference [20] is added, with the integer-exponent remark; 9.52 is labelled as an observed grid maximum.
(4) Conjecture R: a note records that a proposed FOZ proof of the upper bound is under forum discussion and is not verified here.
No other statement changed.
title: The Báez-Duarte subspace has codimension equal to the number of zeta zeros off the critical line, with distance and rate bounds not assuming RH
